Hi Emily — really appreciate the sample and the clear scope. High-level reply below and a concrete next-steps checklist. I’ve also uploaded our recommended benchmark template and model recs to the Drive link (see related_links). Attached: redwood_model_recommendations.pdf and an SOW draft for timeline/roles.

Quick model shortlist (starting point):
- Llama-2-70b-chat (q8_0) — strong few-shot instruction-following, good baseline for summarization.
- Falcon-40b-instruct (q4_k) — competitive on instruction tasks with lower cost; worth validating on triage precision.
- Mistral-22B (quantized q4) — cost-efficient middle ground for throughput-sensitive routes.

Why these: diversity in architecture helps surface different hallucination profiles and token-efficiency trade-offs. We recommend running the same prompt bank across all three with identical decoding settings and a human adjudication tier for borderline cases.

Suggested eval plan on Redwood (concise):
1) Data ingest: you provide S3 or Drive export of the full seedset + metadata. Required format: CSV with columns: id, input, expected_output, task_type (triage|summary), source_context (optional), severity_tag (optional).
2) Config: pin model version + quantization profile; use Redwood "eval-runner" with fixed decoding: top_p=0.92, temp=0.0 for triage, temp=0.2 for summarization, max_tokens set per task_type.
3) Scoring: automated pass tiers + human review. Automated metrics: exact match rate (triage), ROUGE-L + semantic similarity (summaries) measured with embedding cosine (threshold 0.78). Human review for false positives/negatives and hallucination rate sampling (5% stratified).
4) Regression checks: include a null-set (known hallucination cases) and a calibration set from your historical logs to measure drift.
5) Deliverables: per-model scorecard, confusion matrix for triage labels, qualitative failure log, recommended model+config, and a short-run latency/cost table.

Operational asks from VantageHealth:
- Provide access to S3 bucket or shared Drive with the full dataset (we only need read access for the eval-run).
- Confirm the two task definitions in a one-pager (we’ll reuse your CSV task_type).
- Stakeholder availability for a 30-min kickoff to agree pass thresholds.

Timeline: 2–3 business days for infra/setup after we have dataset access; 7–10 days for a full quantitative run + sampling and human adjudication.

Next steps checklist (action owners):
- Emily: share S3 link and confirm task_type definitions.
- Ava: create eval project in Redwood, upload runner templates, schedule kickoff.
- Ben / Marissa: prepare scorer harness and quick lint of dataset.

If this looks good I’ll schedule a 30-min slot Thursday or Friday.

Best,
Ava Chen
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: VantageHealth — technical eval spec and runner details

Thanks — following up with the technical spec and some pragmatic guardrails. Below are the pieces my team will run and what we’ll need from your side.

Eval runner / infra notes (no attachments):
- Redwood eval-runner config: concurrency=16, batch_policy=dynamic, kv_cache=true. We'll set a per-request timeout of 6s for triage flows and 12s for summarization.
- Model pinning: we’ll pin the exact model commit hash (we’ll supply these in the Drive doc). Please expect minor throughput differences between the three candidates; we’ll report p50/p95 token latency.
- Quantization: run the q8_0 build for Llama-2-70b-chat as baseline; also run q4_k for Falcon-40b-instruct. If memory permits we’ll run Mistral-22B q4.

Scoring harness (what we will compute automatically):
- Triage: label-level exact-match, top-1 accuracy, confusion matrix, precision/recall per label. Pass threshold: >= 92% top-1 accuracy on high-confidence subset (confidence > 0.85).
- Summaries: ROUGE-L, BERTScore, and embedding cosine similarity (use sent-emb-avg). Pass threshold: embedding cosine >= 0.78 on gold summaries and <= 2% hallucination rate by sampling.
- Safety/Regressions: run safety filter (policy-check) and hallucination probe suite. We’ll flag any model with hallucination failure rate > 2% for human review.

Human adjudication:
- We’ll set up a lightweight panel (3 reviewers) for disputed cases and provide an adjudication rubric (clarity, factuality, relevance). Expect ~3–4 business days for a 3k-sample adjudication if we run ~1k samples through human review.

Data and access requests (from VantageHealth):
- S3 read role ARN or Drive share link; if S3 provide path and IAM role for read-only access.
- A quick mapping doc that defines target labels for triage and any entity normalization rules.
- Any PII redaction wishes (we’ll mask PHI by default).

Estimated timeline & effort:
- Infra + small smoke run: 48–72 hours after we get access.
- Full automated run (3 models, 3k rows): ~24 hours compute time + reporting.
- Human adjudication and final deliverables: additional 3–5 business days.

Action items:
- Marissa: provision runner and prepare scorer harness.
- Ben: prepare cost estimate and add to the SOW.
- Emily: share access + label mapping.
